content.text:
Done. Three PNGs are in the working folder at exactly the requested sizes.

**Approach:** one parametric HTML template (`build.js` emits `portrait.html` / `wide.html` / `sky.html`) where every type size, icon size, padding and gap is `calc(var(--s) * Npx)`, with `--s` = 1 / 0.85 / 0.28. So the whole design scales from a single master rather than being hand-tuned three times.

**How the requirements were met at all sizes:**
- **Full-width bands** — the photo band and red CTA bar are direct children of the flex column with no horizontal padding (padding lives on a `.pad` class applied only to text sections), so they span the viewport edge-to-edge at 1080, 1200 and 300.
- **Photo crops, never distorts** — `object-fit: cover` with `object-position: 32% 58%` to keep the farmhouse and sun in frame even in the narrow 300px crop. Verified natural 1600×1000 rendering into 1080×496, 1200×341 and 300×260.
- **Vertical fit** — the photo band is the flexible element (`flex: 6 1 …`) and the inter-section gaps absorb the rest, so the 0.85× content fits 1000px tall and the 0.28× content fills 600px without stranding whitespace. Measured gaps come out uniform at each size (≈51px portrait, ≈30px wide, ≈34px sky).

**Verification:** rather than eyeballing, I wrote `audit.js` to measure the live DOM at each viewport. It reported **no out-of-viewport elements, no document scroll, and `scrollWidth == clientWidth` on every nowrap text run** (candidate names, "VOTE BY MAIL", steps, footer), plus evenly spaced columns (gaps 22 / 18.7 / 6.2px, equal widths). I also upscaled the sky render to confirm the 0.28× text is clean and non-overlapping.

Two notes worth flagging:
- My first audit run silently used the default 1280×720 viewport (I'd passed `viewportSize` instead of `viewport` to `newPage`), so its numbers were meaningless. I caught it from the `1280` values in the output and re-ran — the results above are from the corrected run.
- The audit still reports one benign item: `h1` scrollHeight exceeds clientHeight by ~3px. That's glyph ink extending past a tight `line-height: 1.08` box, not a clip — nothing has `overflow: hidden` there and the following gap is 30px+, so there's no visual cut-off or overlap. I left the tight leading since it makes the headline read as one block.
